newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses direction on arb selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses direction on arb selling.

text.p: LIFFE's robusta coffee futures reversed earlier upward direction to end mostly down but off lows on arbitrage selling against New York, traders said.
The selling in London emerged after the March contract in New York failed to trigger sell-stops below 108 U.S. cents a lb earlier in the afternoon.
This sparked fresh covering in New York but prices have fallen back since to a low of 107.50.
London's benchmark March position was just $2 down on the day at $1,262 a tonne. It had touched a high of $1,275 and a low of $1,252.
Except for front-month January which firmed $1 to $1,332, other remaining months were $8 down.
London values were buoyed early by follow-through buying after impressive New York gains on Tuesday.
Today's slide in London was not accompanied by big volume and traders said most players were wary of unloading their long positions as the market tried to retrace from its recent lows.
There were no immediate market-moving news. Traders said all eyes would focus on U.S. Department of Agriculture 1996/97 coffee balance estimates due to be released on Friday.
This would be followed by the U.S. Green Coffee Association coffee stock data are due on Monday, along with London's certified coffee figures for November.
No changes are expected in the USDA figures but traders would not rule out any surprises.
The USDA could revise its 1996/97 crop estimate for Brazil of 27.5 million 60-kg bags and make preliminary crop forecast for Brazil's 1997/87 season, traders said.
Elsewhere, news Brazil exported 1.59 million bags of coffee in November was within trade expectation.
Traders also showed no immediate reaction to news large German roaster Tchibo Holding AG planned to buy another German roaster Eduscho GmbH and Co.
"The rumour has been around in Germany for some time," said one.
